features.title: E2E stability: mixer focus guard + WebView2 isolation + zombie cleanup
features.user_visible_behavior: The Windows Tauri E2E matrix stops flaking with "No window could be found" after consecutive app restarts: the mixer keeps its window open under the debug marker (auto-close-on-blur is production-only), each surface app gets an isolated WebView2 user-data folder so orphaned renderer processes from force-killed runs cannot corrupt the next webview, and the E2E wrapper kills leftover app instances before and after every run — which also removes the stale native-HUD ghost a killed E2E app can leave on the desktop.

features.title: FE-BE connection stability: non-blocking polls and backend health events
features.user_visible_behavior: Webview surfaces never freeze or appear disconnected when the audio backend hiccups: IPC commands are never queued behind the host poll threads (they skip a cycle instead of blocking on the AppCore mutex), and backend failures publish a one-shot Ready ↔ Degraded status so the mixer shows a live 'Audio backend temporarily unavailable' notice instead of silently freezing on stale values; recovery publishes Ready and resumes live updates.
verification: host_core integration: backend_degradation_publishes_one_shot_status_and_recovers — a failing probe emits exactly one backend:degraded event, no fabricated volume event, repeat probes stay silent, recovery emits backend:ready and resumes publishing (25/25 host_core tests).
host_core integration: bootstrap_reports_degraded_backend_when_the_probe_fails — BootstrapPayload.backend_status reflects the initial probe.

src-tauri polls use try_lock: the 20 ms hotkey poll and the 150 ms config/audio poll skip their cycle when a command holds AppCore, so commands never wait behind a possibly-blocking get_state (PulseAudio/CoreAudio/WASAPI).
TauriSink::backend emits state://backend; the mixer listens and renders the notice from live events and from a degraded bootstrap (2 new Vitest tests; frontend 99/99).
